verdict.rationale: LM Studio documents llmster, a headless daemon that runs without the desktop app, which is the closest thing to a lightweight runtime here. A community user contrasts headless use with the 'big chonky Electron UI'. Nothing in the evidence measures or claims fast cold-start or time-to-first-inference, and on-demand loading only says models load before the request returns. Missing for 10: documented cold-start or startup-latency figures, binary size or footprint details, and independent hands-on benchmarks of llmster startup speed.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can get a fast cold start from a lightweight runtime binary instead of waiting seconds before inference begins

citations.quote: llmster is the headless version of LM Studio, no desktop app required.
llmster is LM Studio's headless daemon for servers, cloud instances, and CI.
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
